title: REDEC
text: This github directory is used for cartographic experiments in relation with the submission of the REDEC project to the AAPG 2026 of the ANR. We will more precisely focus onthe analysis of four cases studies related to the département of Isère, Maine-et-Loire, Somme and Val-de-Marne.

title: REDEC
text:
Selection of cases studies
Four département has been carefully chosen as places of experiment of the different methods and concepts developed in previous work packages. These four case studies will be used ex-ante in order to test methods and concepts that will be further applied to the whole territory of France. They will also be used ex-post as proof of concept for researcher and decision maker. And finally they will be used as test for the research of the best way to disseminate the results toward stakeholders and citizens. To achieve this objectives, the four cases studies has been chosen in order to represent both geographical complexity and political diversity of situations :
– Val-de-Marne (94) is a metropolitan département located in the suburb of Paris with a very high population density concentrated in very few communes which implies necessarily to break some of them in order to have equal population size in cantons. The political opinion is characterized by equivalent proportion of votes for left and center-right but very few votes for far-right.
– Isère (38) offers the case of a département which combines very strong geographical and political differences. The density of population is very high in the metropolitan agglomeration of Grenoble and the related valleys but very low in mountains area. The political diversity is complete with far-right in the north, far-left in the suburb of Grenoble and center-left or center right elsewhere.
– Somme (80) is a good example of rural and industrial area that has been exposed to economic crisis and has recently offers a majority of vote to far-right, with the exception of the capital city of Amiens. Furthermore, the strange shape of some of its districts raises questions. It is also a remarkable case of gerrymandering with three strange circonscriptions having the form of an octopus (n°4) and a salamander (n°1) surrounding a frog (n°2) …
– Maine-et-Loire (49) located in the Western part of France is the opposite example of Somme in political terms as it remains a typical area or resistance of center-right or center-left.It is also characterized by an interesting administrative evolution with a strong reduction of the number of communes by merging (Bideau 2024). We arrive at a moment where some cluster of rural communes are larger than cantons.

title: REDEC
text:
Data collection
We will firstly examine which data can be collected and combine at different levels in each of the selected area.

text:
Experiments
We will then realize preliminary experiments of redisctricting applied to the electoral circonscription. The objective will be to compare the current offcial division against alternative proposals.

title: ANR REDEC - Workpackage E
text:
Objectifs
Le but de la tâche E.1 est de reconstruire la géométrie de l’ensemble des maillages politiques (communes, cantons, circonscriptions, départements) à partir de la brique de base constituée par les bureaux de votes. Plusieurs difficultés doivent être résolus :

title: ANR REDEC - Workpackage E
text:
Difficultés

Choix de la date de référence : la carte des bureaux de vote est en évolution constante et peut changer d’une élection à une autre, généralement par ajout de nouveaux bureaux de vote. En première analyse, on prendra comme référence les élections présidentielles et législatives de 2022.
Incertitudes sur la géométrie des bureaux de vote : il n’existe pas de cartographie précise des contours des bureaux de vote mais une simple liste de rues, sections de trottoirs rattachées à tel ou tel bureau de vote. L’INSEE a proposé une première cartographie des bureaux de vote à partir du fichier des adresses des votants mais ces géométries semblent comporter beaucoup d’erreurs ou d’irrégularités.
Simplification des limites : On souhaite disposer d’un fichier simplifié des contours des bureaux de vote afin de pouvoir plus facilement en déduire leur topologie et effectuer des transformations de type cartogramme (modification des surfaces pour les rendre proportionnelles au nombre d’inscrit). Mais cette simplification doit être aussi juste que possible et ne pas altérer les limites connues avec certitude.

title: ANR REDEC - Workpackage E
section: La carte des bureaux de vote en 2022
text:
La carte des bureaux de vote en 2022
L’INSEE a établi pour la première fois en 2022 une cartographie complète des bureaux de vote en France en se servant du répertoire électoral unique (REU) et de la base des adresses nationales (BAN). La méthodologie rigoureuse est présentée en détail dans le billet de blog publié le 28 juin 2023 et intitulé « A voté » : à chaque bureau de vote ses électeurs.
Ce découpage est a priori en adéquation avec notre objectif puisqu’il est fondé sur la situation des fichiers électoraux en septembre 2022, soit juste après les élections législatives et présidentielles qui ont eu lieu cette année-là.

d. Automatisation
On crée une fonction permettant de répliquer les étpaes décrites ci-dessus

bv_simplify <- function(allbv = bv,
                        mycom="94001",
                        simp = 0.1){

  
  # (0) Extract bv of my commune
  selbv <- allbv %>% filter(comcode==mycom) %>% 
            select(comcode, bvonum) %>%
            arrange(bvonum) %>%
            mutate(bvorder = 1:length(bvonum))
  
  # (1) Create commune border
  selcom<- selbv %>% summarise()
  
  # (2) Simplify
  selbv2<-ms_simplify(selbv,keep = simp)
  
  # (3) Eliminate external area
  selbv3<-ms_clip(target=selbv2, clip=selcom)
  
  # (4) reaffect internal area
    # A helper function that erases all of y from x:
   st_erase = function(x, y) st_difference(x, st_union(st_combine(y)))
   sub<-st_erase(selcom,selbv3)

   # Split multipolygon in simple polygon
   sub<-st_cast(sub,"POLYGON")

   # Find intersections with geometries
   x<-st_intersects(sub,selbv)
   first<-function(x){x[1]}
   sub$bvorder<-as.numeric(lapply(x,first))

   # Add bvonum
   t<- st_drop_geometry(selbv)
   sub<-sub %>% left_join(t) %>% 
     select(comcode,bvonum, bvorder, geometry)
   
   # bind with selbv3
   selbv4 <- rbind(selbv3, sub) %>% 
     group_by(comcode, bvonum) %>%
     summarise()

return(selbv4)
}

Algorithme 1 : Centre représentatif d’une surface
POUR CHAQUE COMMUNE

On charge le contour des bureaux de vote 2022 fourni par l’INSEE

On détermine les centroïdes à l’aide de la fonction st_centroid

title: ANR REDEC - Workpackage E
text:
Algorithme 2 : électeur médian
On décide d’assigner à chaque bureau de vote la localisation d’un électeur médian qui soit le plus proche de l’ensemble des autres électeurs présents dans le bureau de vote. Pour abréger le temps de calcul on va utiliser la distance rectilinéaire (distance de Manhattan) qui permet de simplifier le calcul en le décomposant selon les axes X et Y. Le calcul est effectué sur les adresses \(1..n\),pondérées par le nombre d’électeurs \(\omega\)
\(DX_i = \sum^n_{j=1} \omega_j{\lvert X_i-X_j \rvert }\)
\(DY_i = \sum^n_{j=1} \omega_j{\lvert Y_i-Y_j \rvert }\)
\(ACC_i = \frac{1}{DX_j+DY_j}\)
Le calcul se simplifie avec calcul préalable des médianes pondérées selon les axes X et Y.

 ## Discussion

2. Possibilité d’analyser le redécoupage des circonscriptions législatives de 2010 à l’aide des données CARTELEC en se servant des résultats de l’élection présidentielle de 2007 et des données socio-économiques de l’INSEE qui sont fournies grâce à une intersection avec les IRIS.

title: Distribution of seats by departement for Assemblée Nationale and Senat
text:
This short note aims to examine the distribution of seats in the Sénat and the Assemblée Nationale by département in the Metropolitan area of France (excluding Corsica). We propose to test the following hypothesis :

H1: The correlation between the number of seats and population is more important with past census than the present, due to the lack of recent updates.
H2: The relation between the number of seats and the number of registered population in 2024 is characterised by negative residuals in départements with important population growth in recent years and positive residuals in départements with declining or stable population.
H3: The relation between population and number of seats is much lower in the case of the Sénat.

Comment : The map reveals a clear relationship between the population density of départements and their representation in the Sénat (low density) and the Assemblée Nationale (high density). The départements with better representation in the Sénat belong to what is generally called the “diagonale du vide”, from the Ardennes to the Pyrénées. The départements with better representation in the Assemblée Nationale are typically those where the most important cities and metropolitan areas are located (Paris, Lille, Marseille, Nantes, Bordeaux, Toulouse, Montpellier, Grenoble, …).

The fact that the Senate presents itself as a chamber representing territories rather than citizens is not in itself shocking. Many countries have, in fact, structured their second chamber not on a basis proportional to population but rather to the number of autonomous political entities. For example, each department could send two representatives to the Senate. One could even imagine each department having representation in the Senate proportional to its area, if the word ‘territory’ is taken in its geometric sense. The Gironde, with an area of 9,976 km², would then have almost 100 times as many senators as the department of Paris, with its 105 km². But one might perhaps hesitate to apply this rule to French Guiana and its 83,856 km²…
The real problem with the current situation is that the Senate nevertheless claims to provide representation proportional to the number of citizens, but does so in a completely biased manner, using a system that penalises the most populous departments (see the power-law parameter \(\alpha = 0.73\)) and based on population figures that appear to date back to 1980. This is therefore a false form of proportionality and a manifestly unfair rule, since departments with the same number of representatives in the Senate may have populations varying by a ratio of 1 to 4.
The observed link between population density and over-representation in the Senate, compared with the National Assembly, is largely an artefact. It results from an imperfect proportionality law combined with an outdated census reference framework that favours territories whose populations have grown the least. If one were genuinely to ensure objective representation for the least densely populated territories, a new measure would need to be devised, combining, for example, the share of the population and the share of the departments’ total area according to a precise rule of the following type:
\(Weight_i = (\frac{Area_i}{Total_area})^\mu \times (\frac{Pop_i}{Total_pop})^{1-\mu}\)
But are departments really the best level at which to make decisions?

title: Distribution of seats by departement for Assemblée Nationale and Senat
text:
(D) The legal point of view

The revision of 1966
The definition of the number of seats in Senat was modified in 1966 by the law 66-504 from 12-07-1966. One of the reason of the revision was the modification of the departements of Seine and Seine-et-Oise, replaced by 7 new départements. The consequence of the revision was an increase of the number of sénateurs from 30 to 39 in this area and from 255 to 264 in the metropolitan area of France. We can notice that the increase (+9) of seats was limited to the metropolitan area of Paris, without considerng other départements where population changes could have justify changes.



Revision of senateurs in Paris region, 1966




The revision of 2003
The last revision of the number of seats in Sénat was decided in 2003 in order to take into account demographic changes. But the rule adopted was criticized and contested by left-wing party which asked to the Conseil Constitutionnel a censorship. This censorship was not adopted but it is interesting to look at the motivation of the decision :






The decision 2003-475 DC from Conseil Constitutionnel



Les dispositions combinées de l’article 6 de la Déclaration de 1789 et des articles 3 et 24 de la Constitution imposent au législateur de modifier la répartition par département des sièges de sénateurs pour tenir compte des évolutions de la population des collectivités territoriales dont le Sénat assure la représentation. Pour modifier la répartition par département des sièges de sénateurs figurant au tableau n° 6 annexé à la partie législative du code électoral, le législateur a retenu un système de répartition par tranches, soit un sénateur jusqu’à 150 000 habitants, puis un sénateur supplémentaire par tranche ou fraction de tranche de 250 000 habitants. Si l’application d’un tel système maintient certaines disparités démographiques, les modifications qui résultent de la loi déférée n’en réduisent pas moins sensiblement les inégalités de représentation antérieures. En conservant aux départements de la Creuse et de Paris leur représentation antérieure, le législateur a apporté une dérogation au mode de calcul qu’il avait lui-même retenu. Toutefois, pour regrettable qu’elle soit, cette dérogation, qui intéresse 4 sièges, ne porte pas au principe d’égalité devant le suffrage une atteinte telle qu’elle entacherait d’inconstitutionnalité la loi déférée. Eu égard au rôle confié au Sénat par l’article 24 de la Constitution, la nouvelle répartition des sièges n’est pas contraire à la Constitution.
(2003-475 DC, 24 juillet 2003, cons. 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, Journal officiel du 31 juillet 2003, page 13038)




The rule of 2003 (version 1)
The interest of the judgement of 2003 is to provide an explicit formulation of the rule used for the definition of the number of seats which was formulated as follow :

rule 1 : One seat for each département until 150 000 h
rule 2 : One seat more for each “tranche” or “number of tranche” of 250 000 h

Which can be formalized, if we undestrand correctly by the formula :
\(Y = 1 + round(\frac{X-150000}{250000})\)
If we assume that the law was based on the census of 1999 which was the last available at that time, can we verify that the application was correct with the exceptions of Creuse and Paris ?

title: Distribution of seats by departement for Assemblée Nationale and Senat
text:
Conclusion
The different analysis realized with the power model has revealed that the number of seats in Sénat is clearly not proportional to population and provide a very important advantage to départements with low population which are generally characterized by low density. The coefficient of the power law linking population and seats is clearly lower than 1 which means that the allocation of seats is strongly biased by what the geographers call the MAUP (Modifiable Area Unit Problem). The merging of two departements in one would necessary decrease their number of seats when the splitting would increase the number of seats. It is unfair and certainly not logical.
The legal analysis of the rule of 2003 suggest that the problem is strongly enhanced in the formula used for the allocation of seats. The application of the same rule to the demographic data of 2023 would not change the inequalities revealed by the power model. It is clearly the rule that should be modified.
